questions.explain: RTO is the maximum tolerable outage duration (failure detection to service restoration), while RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss (the age of the data that must be recovered).
options: Both are described as RTO: recovery time objective covers data loss too.
The downtime limit is the RTO (Recovery Time Objective); the data-loss limit is the RPO (Recovery Point Objective).
The downtime limit is the RPO; the data-loss limit is the RTO.
Downtime limits are called fault tolerance and data-loss limits are called disaster recovery.
questions.q: A business says it can tolerate at most 5 minutes of downtime and zero data loss. How are these two requirements described in HA terms?

questions.explain: Automatic failover requires synchronous-commit mode on the target secondary, so the commit is guaranteed hardened on the secondary before the primary acknowledges it.
options: The secondary must be in synchronous-commit mode.
The secondary must use a readable-secondary license and log shipping.
The secondary must be a Failover Cluster Instance sharing the primary's storage.
Automatic failover works with any asynchronous secondary as long as quorum exists.
questions.q: In SQL Server Always On Availability Groups, what is required for a secondary replica to be eligible for automatic failover?

questions.explain: log_send_queue_size is records waiting to leave the primary; redo_queue_size is records received but not yet redone on the secondary, which measures how stale the secondary's data is.
options: log_send_queue_size
log_send_rate
redo_queue_size
last_commit_time
questions.q: You are monitoring an asynchronous AG secondary with sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states. Which column tells you how stale the secondary's data actually is?

questions.explain: An FCI is one SQL Server instance on shared storage across WSFC nodes; since there is a single copy of the data files, a storage failure or corruption affects the instance regardless of which node owns it.
options: Because an FCI has no quorum and therefore cannot fail over automatically.
Because an FCI replicates log records asynchronously between nodes.
Because an FCI uses shared storage, so there is exactly one copy of the data — it protects against server failure, not storage failure.
Because an FCI only protects individual databases, not the whole instance.
questions.q: Why is a Failover Cluster Instance (FCI) NOT a defense against storage failure or database corruption?

questions.explain: The AG listener is a virtual network name and IP managed by the cluster; after failover it moves to the new primary, so apps connecting to the listener name reconnect without configuration changes. Connections specifying ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly can be routed to secondaries.
options: The application's driver re-resolves the old primary's hostname automatically.
The AG listener — a virtual network name and IP that floats to the current primary — is what applications connect to.
WSFC replicates the primary's IP address to all clients via DNS zone transfers.
Connections survive because SQL Server keeps client sockets open across failover.
questions.q: How does an application transparently reach the current primary after an AG failover without a configuration change?
